stories.title: Russia / Ukraine / NATO
stories.detail: Above its own baseline: 13 headlines against a normal of 23.2, and new language today (threaten, warned). That is a change, not just continuing coverage.
stories.why: Two channels: haven demand, and the structural one - sanctions on Russian reserves in 2022 taught central banks that dollar reserves can be frozen, which is a large part of why official-sector gold buying has been so persistent since.
stories.counterweight: Day-to-day headlines are largely priced. The structural bid shows up in central bank demand data, not in a day's price action.
stories.duration: Headlines: days. The reserve-diversification effect: years, and it is arguably the single biggest reason gold has re-rated.
stories.spoken_why: The day to day headlines are priced, but sanctions on reserves are why central banks keep buying gold.
stories.read: Mostly not following - WTI crude, Gold, Silver and 3 others are all going the other way. Either this is already in the price, or something bigger is driving the tape today.

stories.title: Wider Middle East
stories.detail: Above its own baseline: 5 headlines against a normal of 11.7, and new language today (casualties). That is a change, not just continuing coverage.
stories.why: Haven demand, mostly. Moves gold hard on the first day of a genuine escalation and then fades, because the region's conflicts rarely touch US rate expectations directly.
stories.counterweight: Heavily discounted by markets through repetition - a headline that would have moved gold $40 in the first month of a conflict moves it $5 in the ninth.
stories.duration: Hours to days. The shortest-lived of the major flashpoints unless it pulls Iran in directly.
stories.spoken_why: It moves gold on haven demand, but the effect fades fast because these headlines rarely touch US interest rates.
stories.read: Mostly not following - Gold, WTI crude, Silver and 3 others are all going the other way. Either this is already in the price, or something bigger is driving the tape today.

stories.title: US / Israel – Iran
stories.detail: 7 headlines, which is about its normal of 31.5 after 30 days running. Continuing coverage rather than escalation - gold has priced this.
stories.why: The one flashpoint that hits gold through every channel at once. Safe-haven bid on the headline, Treasuries bid so nominal and real yields fall, and - uniquely - a credible threat to the Strait of Hormuz spikes crude, which lifts inflation expectations. Roughly a fifth of seaborne oil passes through that strait.
stories.counterweight: The dollar is also a haven, so risk-off bids the dollar too and cancels part of gold's gain. This is why some escalation days produce a far smaller gold move than the headlines imply.
stories.duration: Days. Gold spikes on the exchange of fire and gives most of it back within a week unless the oil disruption is real and sustained, because only then does it reach the Fed's reaction function.
stories.spoken: Iran, and the US and Israel
stories.spoken_why: It reaches gold through three channels at once: the haven bid, lower real yields, and the risk to oil coming through the Strait of Hormuz.
stories.read: Mostly not following - WTI crude, Gold, Silver and 3 others are all going the other way. Either this is already in the price, or something bigger is driving the tape today.

stories.title: China / Taiwan
stories.detail: 6 headlines, which is about its normal of 12.4 after 15 days running. Continuing coverage rather than escalation - gold has priced this.
stories.why: Low frequency, very high severity. A genuine blockade or invasion scenario is the largest single tail risk in the gold market, because it would be a global supply-chain and reserve-currency event simultaneously.
stories.counterweight: Routine incursions and drills are so frequent they carry almost no information. Gold ignores them, correctly.
stories.duration: Drills: nothing. A real blockade: a regime change in gold pricing, not a spike.
stories.spoken_why: Routine drills mean nothing, but a genuine blockade would be the largest single risk in this market.
stories.read: Broadly consistent, though Gold, EUR/USD are not playing along. One asset out of line is usually its own story; several is a reason to doubt the read.

affairs.caveat: Expected direction is derived from the driver model; observed is what prices have actually done. Many things move at once, so this is a consistency check rather than attribution.

asia.read: Asian equities are broadly lower, averaging -1.30%. Risk came off overnight, which normally gives gold a small bid into London. Gold moved -1.60% overnight in a 2.93% range, and comes into London near the bottom of it. Sitting on the lows into the open leaves it vulnerable to a flush if London sells it. 2 minor Asian releases overnight, none of them the kind that reaches gold.
asia.caveat: Measured from 00:00 UK to 16:01. Tokyo closes around 07:00 UK and Hong Kong around 09:00, so this is a session finishing rather than one that has finished.

correlations.regime: Gold and the dollar are running at -0.21. The usual inverse link has weakened, which normally means something other than the currency is setting gold - haven flow or official buying. Against the S&P it is +0.56. Gold is trading WITH risk assets rather than against them, so it is behaving as a liquidity asset right now, not a hedge - do not rely on it to offset an equity drawdown while that holds.

profile.name: CB Consumer Confidence
profile.what: Survey of household sentiment about business and labour conditions. Released 15:00 UK.
profile.why_gold: A soft indicator of future spending. Rarely moves gold on its own.
profile.watch: The labour differential - jobs plentiful minus jobs hard to get - which tracks the unemployment rate.
profile.gotchas: Sentiment surveys have decoupled from actual spending behaviour for years now.
